acceptance: A test that forces the first git exec in gittest to fail with EBADF passes after one retry, and one that fails twice still fails naming the error (red first)
ship's captureWithEBADFRetry and gittest share one retry rule, with no second copy
A persistent non-EBADF error from git is never retried
fix: Move the once-only EBADF and closed-pipe retry from ship's test helper into gittest's command runner (Repo.Git and the fixture's init), so every real-git test gets it, and have ship's tests use that one rule.
summary: TestShipFromWorktree_DiffCachedQuietFails_Errors failed on ubuntu-latest with `gittest: git init -q -b main ...: fork/exec /usr/bin/git: bad file descriptor` in a PR that does not touch ship or gittest. The EBADF race in real-git test runners is already a documented class (docs/architecture/packages/internal-phases-ship.md: captureWithEBADFRetry, first seen on macOS CI), but only one ship test path retries; the shared gittest helper, used across packages, does not. This is the second sighting of the class, now on Linux.
title: Give the shared gittest git runner the EBADF retry that one ship test path already has
